tagline.text: The heart of Samar: the Philippines' largest old-growth forest, limestone caves and whitewater rivers

location.label: Location
location.text: Interior of Samar, Eastern Samar and Northern Samar (about 2 hours overland from Tacloban)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,500~5,000 (per person, per day, including guide and transport)

children.text: A protected area of about 333,000 hectares in the middle of Samar, the largest terrestrial protected area in the Philippines. Sohoton Natural Bridge, the Calbiga caves, rapids boating on the Ulot River and old-growth forest where the Philippine eagle lives are all found in one place.
Samar Island Natural Park (SINP) protects the low but rugged central mountain range of Samar Island. The core zone covers about
333,300 hectares

and the buffer zone about 458,700 hectares, together roughly a third of the island, and it is known as the largest contiguous old-growth forest and the largest terrestrial protected area in the Philippines. It spans more than 40 municipalities across Samar, Eastern Samar and Northern Samar provinces, and the nearest major city is Tacloban.

The park began as a forest reserve in 1996, was upgraded to a natural park in 2003 by Proclamation No. 442, and is also described as a national park under the 2018 Expanded NIPAS Act (Republic Act No. 11038). Several areas that were once protected separately now lie inside it: Sohoton Natural Bridge Park, Calbiga Caves Park, Taft Forest, Jicontol Forest and the Bulosao watershed. It is also the source of 25 river watersheds, so it works as a water tank that supplies drinking and irrigation water to people across the island.

The forest ranges from lowland mixed dipterocarp forest to forest over limestone and mossy cloud forest. Samar belongs to the Eastern Visayas and Mindanao biogeographic region, which holds many endangered and endemic species, and Taft Forest in this park is known as a nesting site of the Philippine eagle. The Philippine tarsier, the Philippine flying lemur and birds such as the Samar hornbill also live here.

For a traveler, this park is less a single attraction than a huge area with several entry points. On the Basey side you travel by boat up the Sohoton River to see the natural bridge and caves, on the Paranas side you ride the rapids of the Ulot River by boat, and on the Calbiga side you can explore the Langun-Gobingob caves, ranked among the largest in the Philippines. Facilities are modest, but you get nature that has been touched far less by people, which suits travelers who like adventure.
From Basey, a boat ride of
about 15-30 minutes
up the Sohoton River brings you to a huge limestone arch, the natural bridge, and the Panhulugan caves. This is the easiest part of the park to reach, and more detail is in the
Sohoton Natural Bridge National Park
entry.

This cave system in Calbiga is said to cover about 2,968 hectares and to consist of 12 caves including Langun, Gobingob, Lurodpon and Bitong Mahangin. Described as the largest cave in the Philippines, it is a specialist trip: you hike to the entrance and then spend half a day or more underground.
On the Ulot River in Paranas, a small boat takes you along a stretch of
about 21 km
. Curtain-like waterfalls, sharp bends in the gorge and splashing rapids follow one after another, and you should expect to get wet.

Taft Forest is known as a nesting site of the Philippine eagle, and Jicontol Forest is part of an important bird area with restricted-range species such as the Samar hornbill, the Visayan broadbill and the yellow-breasted tailorbird. Your chances of seeing birds are much better with a specialist guide.

This waterfall in Calbiga spreads wide as it tumbles down and is called the little Niagara of Samar. You reach it by motorcycle taxi and a short walk, so it combines well with a cave trip. Access rules should be confirmed locally.

The waters of large watersheds such as Suribao, Can-avid, Dolores, Catubig, Gandara and Taft begin in this park. Following a river downstream brings clear water, boulders and rapids, which makes for fun river travel.

The road running from Paranas toward Taft in Eastern Samar crosses the middle of the forest. Dense forest lines the road, giving a sense of the park's scale, and along the way there are turnoffs to the park headquarters and the boat landing.
Take a jeepney or van to Basey from the Tacloban New Bus Terminal (Abucay). The ride takes
about 40-60 minutes
Register for entry and arrange a boat at the Basey Tourism Office. A guide is required, so stop here first.
Put on a life jacket and travel up the Sohoton River for
about 15-30 minutes
. The water is clear and limestone cliffs rise on both sides.
Tour the natural bridge and the Panhulugan caves with a guide. You need a flashlight in the caves, and you can also arrange a lighting service for an extra fee.
Have lunch and return by boat.
See Basey Church and the shops selling woven crafts, then return to Tacloban.
The Sohoton section is the easiest part of the park, so I recommend this course for first-time visitors.
From Tacloban, head toward Catbalogan along the Maharlika Highway.
After entering Paranas, turn onto the Wright-Taft Road at Buray Junction (the corner with a gas station). The park headquarters is
about 16 km
away.
Board the torpedo boat at the Campo Uno landing in Barangay Tenani. Swim at the rest stop downstream, then return against the rapids upstream.
Rest at the lodging at park headquarters or go tubing in a nearby stream.
Have a simple dinner at a shop near the headquarters. There are few eateries, so prepare food in advance.
Do some light birdwatching to the sounds of the forest, then head to Tacloban or Catbalogan.
Operations and fees change from year to year, so ask the park office or the Paranas tourism office before you go.
Travel from Catbalogan or Tacloban to Calbiga, confirm the schedule and permits with a local operator, and stay overnight.

Starting from Barangay Panayuran, hike a little over 1 hour to the cave entrance. The one-day course is said to spend about 4 hours underground (2-6 hours depending on the route), exit through a different opening, and then climb for about 3 hours (the climb time is from a 2015 trip report).
Visit Lulugayan Falls, rest, and move on.
Cave exploration requires permits, a professional guide and equipment. The schedule may be canceled in the rainy season or right after heavy rain.
There are direct flights from Ninoy Aquino International Airport in Manila to Tacloban (TAC), and the flight takes about
1 hour 20 minutes
. Airlines and schedules change often, so check when you book.
From the airport, take a taxi or tricycle into Tacloban.
You can go overland from Manila, but with the ferry crossing included it takes close to a full day.
Take a jeepney or van bound for Basey from the Tacloban New Bus Terminal. It takes
about 40-60 minutes
, and you get off in front of the Basey Tourism Office.
After registering at the tourism office, take a boat for
about 15-30 minutes
to reach the Sohoton area.

items.title: Tacloban to Paranas (Ulot River and park headquarters)

children.text: Drive along the Maharlika Highway toward Catbalogan and enter Paranas. Turn onto the Wright-Taft Road at Buray Junction, where there is a gas station, and the park headquarters is
about 16 km
away.
Public transport is infrequent, so a rental car or a hired vehicle is recommended. The road is concrete but has potholes in places.
Calbiga is
about 50-65 km
from Tacloban, or
1.5-2 hours
by car. From Catbalogan it takes about
1 hour 30 minutes
by bus.
To reach Barangay Panayuran, where the cave trail begins, take a motorcycle from Calbiga town.
Between towns, motorcycle taxis (habal-habal) and tricycles are the norm.
Inside the park there are almost no roads and rivers and forest paths are the main routes, so a guide is essential.

Samar has a lot of rain through the year and lies in the path of typhoons. Because river and cave activities are central here, it matters to schedule your trip for a drier period. When rivers rise, boat and cave tours may be suspended.
Generally
March–June
is described as the most stable period, and cave exploration is often run in the dry season of
November–May
. The weather differs from year to year, so check the forecast for the days before you leave.

rows: Frequent rain and cool, affected by the northeast monsoon and typhoons

There are almost no hotels inside the park, so most travelers stay in towns such as Tacloban, Catbalogan or Calbiga. Tacloban has the most lodging and restaurants and allows day trips to Basey. On the Ulot River side, the park headquarters is known to run a dormitory and small rooms, but facilities and rates can change, so check in advance.

There are almost no restaurants near the park entrances, only small shops. It is wise to prepare packed meals, water and snacks in advance. You can try Samar seafood and coconut dishes at restaurants in town.
For Sohoton in Basey, registration at the tourism office comes first. Arrange the boat and guide there all at once.
Carry plenty of cash. Entrance and guide fees are generally paid in cash, and many places have weak signal.
Always wear a life jacket, and bring a waterproof bag, a change of clothes, a towel and a headlamp.
Trekking shoes are a must for cave exploring. Slippers or sandals can be pulled off in the guano mud.
You will definitely get wet on the Ulot River boat. Put your camera and phone in waterproof cases.
Schedules can be canceled by the weather, so leave at least a day of slack.
Start early in the morning whenever possible to avoid the busiest hours.
Park entry rules and fees change often, so check the latest announcements and ask the local tourism office.
Calbiga cave exploring is a demanding activity with vertical sections, a rappel of about 40 m, waist-deep water and slippery mud. Do not enter without a licensed professional guide.
The park is a protected area, so collecting, cutting trees and capturing wildlife without permission are prohibited. Carry all your trash out.
Bat droppings (guano) lie deep in the caves, which makes them slippery and smelly, and snakes have been seen there. People with weak lungs should be careful.
Rivers can rise suddenly after rain. If the guide recommends stopping, always follow.
Mobile signal is poor in the island's interior, so tell your lodging or family your plans before you leave.
Security conditions and travel restrictions in this area can differ from time to time. Check local announcements before you leave.
About
15-30 minutes
by boat from Basey, the park's most representative visitor section.
A base city with the airport, lodging and restaurants, about
45 minutes to 2 hours
from most park entry points.
A long bridge linking Samar and Leyte that you cross on the way from Tacloban into Samar.
The main city of Eastern Samar, a base when approaching the park from the east.
